name: Claude Code
description: Tells Claude Code that Polter is here: registers the MCP server under the user scope and mirrors Polter's skills into ~/.claude/skills/polter-*. Without it an agent has the socket and the token in its environment and no way to use either.

contains: Interrupted · What should Claude do instead?

scope.title: Which Claude Code scope to register in
scope.description: user puts the server in ~/.claude.json for every directory; local puts it in this machine's project entry only. user is the point of doing this at all -- a project scope is exactly the case that already worked.

skills.title: Install skills as well
skills.description: yes mirrors Polter's skills into ~/.claude/skills/polter-*. Claude Code matches its own skills against what the user asked for; Polter's skill_read has to be thought of first, which is why a supervisor told to mind some terminals reaches for a subagent instead. no registers the MCP server and takes back the polter-* skills an earlier yes installed; skills you wrote yourself are never touched.

rules.title: Write Polter's note into this CLI's rules file
rules.description: yes writes a marked block into the user-level rules file (never a project one) saying that what an agent prints reaches nobody, and pointing at the operating-a-terminal skill. It is there because a skill is matched against what the user asked for and nothing matches "you have just finished a task": on real records, 71 tasks produced 15 done reports. Everything outside the markers is left untouched, and no takes the block back out.

tui.title: Which renderer a session Polter starts begins in
tui.description: fullscreen is Claude Code's flicker-free alt-screen renderer (the same as its own `tui: "fullscreen"`); classic is its main-screen renderer, which is what Claude Code calls `"default"`. follow writes neither, so a session Polter starts is rendered however your own ~/.claude/settings.json says -- pick this if you use /tui yourself and want Polter to stay out of it. Only sessions Polter starts are affected: your own settings file is read by this plugin and never written to.

autoScrollEnabled.title: Follow new output with the viewport
autoScrollEnabled.description: on scrolls the conversation back to the bottom whenever new output arrives, so a session you scrolled up in is pulled down again; off leaves the viewport where you put it, with a "1 new message" badge to scroll down to. It only means anything in fullscreen, where Claude Code has a scrollback of its own to be scrolled. follow writes nothing, so your own setting decides. The default is off: measured on 2.1.310, on and off are the same while the viewport is at the bottom, and they differ only once you have scrolled up -- which is the case this is here for.
